nodes.label: mac2
nodes.note: shares a host with mac; placement evidence only

supported: A fabric of three nodes placed a concurrent burst across all three labels, with zero failed requests.
With one node stopped, the remaining nodes served every request; with two stopped, the third served every request. No client saw a failure.
GET /v1/models on the proxy returned the union of the models held by its nodes.
Naming a model placed the request only on a node that holds it: the 3B landed solely on the Windows node, the 1B solely on the two macOS nodes.
Every prompt in every arm was unique, so no number here can be a prefill-cache artefact.
Two nodes on two machines served more requests per second than the faster of them alone: 1.33x, 95% CI [1.17, 1.50] over five paired rounds with zero failed requests.
not_supported: Any scaling number drawn from the third node. Nodes 2 and 3 share one machine, which is the arrangement #652 refused to draw a claim from.

The together_vs_sum_of_singles ratio as a scaling result. It is above 1.0 here, which is impossible for independent placement and is an artefact of the concurrency chosen: each node reports continuous_batch_slots=2 and every arm was driven at concurrency 4, so a single-node arm had 4 requests in flight against 2 slots and queued the rest, while the two-node arm had 4 against 4. The single-node denominators are therefore depressed. together_vs_best_single is the sound comparison.
Any claim about a lane other than the one recorded per node in this bundle.
Any comparison between the two machines as hardware: they ran different execution lanes and different thread counts, both recorded. The Windows node ran a CPU lane here, not its CUDA lane.
Any throughput claim for the second model. The throughput arms were run on the 1B only; the 3B appears in this bundle for placement and model-routing evidence, not for throughput.
claims.honest_sentence: Three nodes is met for placement; the throughput arms are two machines, because the third node shares a host.
method: Arms are interleaved and their order rotated each round; ratios are taken within a round.
A unique marker leads every prompt.
Per-node attribution is read from the x-camelid-fabric-node response header, never inferred.
The execution lane is read from /v1/health execution_plan.selected_backend before and after each campaign.
One warm-up round per model is discarded.
A run containing any failed request is not reported as a throughput number.
